verdict: Below threshold (5.5 < 7.5): revise before submission. The paper is an unusually honest, internally consistent pre-registered characterisation, but its substantive findings are confined to one stay-and-probe cell that largely removes the travel-cost coupling motivating the study, the amortization question in the title ends inconclusive (the exploratory long-training student reopens it), H2 is a low-power non-detection on an objective that misorders the teacher, and the cost claim lacks a matched-latency comparison against reduced-size planners. Hedging is so dense that the takeaway is hard to extract. Several gaps can be closed from existing data, but reaching a top-venue bar requires new evidence, chiefly a cell where travel binds.
strengths: Rigorous pre-registration: hypotheses, thresholds, outcome map and fail-branch readings were frozen before test, the routing to outcome row 4 is fully documented (Appendix A, Table A1), and descoped items are listed with the reason.

Candid scoping throughout: the paper explicitly identifies the stay-and-probe regime (6.1 deg mean travel, 79.3 % zero moves) and restricts every claim to it, and it separates exploratory post-freeze rows (long-training student, B-fan) from registered tests.

Controlled learnability comparison: identical belief-free DeepSets head, action set and feasibility masking for DAgger distillation and PPO, with paired episodes and a crossed episode x seed bootstrap.

Useful behavioural diagnosis (Table 2d): it shows RL converges to a qualitatively different three-probe, travel-heavy strategy, while the student collapses toward B-fan-like stay-and-fan behaviour. This explains the numbers better than success alone would.

The H3 headroom estimator has instrument checks (a notch construction with an exact gap, a zero-gap bank, a one-sided bias guard), and its limits (selection bias of V_LA, coarse completion sub-grid, incomplete same-angle offset screen) are stated openly.
The latency decomposition (Table 2c) gives a clean structural argument for why candidate pruning cannot reach 10x: particle-filter work outside scoring caps the speed-up.

The ball-sPCE vs grid-BI ordering inversion is a genuinely useful negative observation about contrastive RL objectives for localization, and the cap-saturation check rules out the obvious explanation.
Numbers are internally consistent across abstract, text, tables and appendix (e.g., G(12), student/RL/G* deltas, long-student deltas, latency ratios).
weaknesses: [evidence-level] All learning results and the headline H3 bound come from a single cell (S, kappa = 12, n* = 4) that the paper itself shows is a stay-and-probe regime. The motivating phenomenon (a finger stranded far from the informative region, travel coupling breaking submodularity) barely occurs, so the paper cannot answer its own framing question for the regime where it matters.

[evidence-level] The amortization question is unresolved. D3 failed, but the exploratory 200-epoch student is within -1.7 pp of G* (ci95 [-6.8, +3.4]) and improved held-out regret on every seed. So the registered failure may be an artefact of the stopping rule and the unmatched optimisation budgets (student rounds of 4-16 epochs and seconds of wall time vs 200,064 PPO episodes per seed).

[evidence-level] H2 has low power (80 % power only near a true delta of 0.57 nats, three seeds, wide seed-dominated intervals), and it is decided on ball-sPCE, which orders G* below both learners while grid BI orders it above. The registered rejection therefore carries little information about localization quality.

[evidence-level] The cost claim (about 2,200x per decision) is against full-size G* only. The provisional reduced-size frontier (Table 2e) is incomplete (155-186 of 200 episodes), on pilot3 rather than test3, timed under a different procedure, and never paired with the learners at matched latency, so what amortization buys is not established.

[evidence-level] The H3 instrument lacks an in-domain positive control. The 32-action screen does not guarantee coverage of the same-angle offsets that matter most in this regime, the completion's coarse angular sub-grid handicap is unquantified, V_LA selection bias is unmeasured, and the bias check (V_G* read 4.3 % low, comparable to the 0.041-nat gap) mixes policy and filter-implementation differences.

[evidence-level] Comparators are not shown tuned. Both the RL and distillation sweeps used 4 configurations on 1 seed, and both selected the largest learning rate in their grids, so optima may lie outside the grid. The belief-input control is under-fit (train top-1 0.33-0.36) and isolates nothing about representation.

[evidence-level] The evaluator is not shown converged (the sub-4 to sub-8 gate failed; 7.5 % of S0 calibration outcomes flip; no finer grid checked). Yet several key success differences are only a few points.

[paper-level] Contributions are thin relative to a top venue. C1 is a replication of a previously known estimate against a threshold set with that estimate in hand. C2/C3 are non-detections. C4 is a back-of-envelope latency argument. None yields a method or a clear positive finding.

[paper-level] Readability is poor. Nearly every sentence carries multiple qualifiers, the abstract and introduction are dense with gate bookkeeping (thresholds, ci bounds, 'not shown to differ', 'equivalence was not tested'), and a reader struggles to extract the main message. Much of this belongs in Section 7 or Appendix A.

[paper-level] The title and framing ('Can ... Be Amortized?') promise an answer the single-cell, inconclusive result cannot deliver. The paper would be more accurate framed as a characterisation of a stay-and-probe regime and a caution about proxy objectives and unmatched budgets.

[paper-level] Several pre-registered or easily computed analyses of existing data are missing. The top-2 near-tie fraction is not computed although full G* score vectors are stored. Training compute (including teacher labelling) is not reported. There is no per-episode correlation of g_T with grid BI to explain the inversion, and no variance decomposition for the H2 interval.

[paper-level] The latency bound attributes 15.0 % of G* time to assimilation plus neighbour lists (0.137 s of 0.9135 s), but the component medians sum to only 0.854 s. The unattributed ~0.06 s outside scoring is not discussed. If it is non-scoring work, the pruning ceiling is about 4.6x rather than 6.7x. The conclusion is unchanged, but the bound should be stated precisely.

[paper-level] Test3 has been reused by two post-freeze exploratory rows, so later claims on that split lose their confirmatory character. This is acknowledged but weakens the exploratory long-student result that the conclusion leans on.
required_actions: [evidence-level] Run at least one cell in which travel binds (e.g., lower kappa with a larger budget, a larger n*, or the asymmetric set A) and repeat H3 and the student/RL comparison there. Without it, the paper's motivating question is untested.

[evidence-level] Match optimisation budgets between the learners. Run the long-training (or budget-matched) student under the registered D3 rule on val3 with more episodes and seeds, and report a budget-matched learning curve for both distillation and PPO.

[evidence-level] Complete the reduced-size G* runs and evaluate them on test3, paired with the learners and timed under the Table 2c latency protocol, so the accuracy-latency comparison is made at matched latency rather than against full-size G* only.

[evidence-level] Strengthen the H3 instrument. Add a complete screen of all offsets at the current finger angle (or a full-action screen), an in-domain positive control on the touch task with a planted gap, a measurement of V_LA selection bias (e.g., independent re-estimation of the selected action), and a bias check whose reference differs from the estimator in policy only.

[evidence-level] Increase the number of seeds for both learners (at least 5-10) and widen both hyperparameter sweeps beyond the largest learning rate tested, so the comparators can be shown tuned and H2 or a TOST has useful power.

[evidence-level] Evaluate held-out regret on student-visited states (label student rollouts with G*) to test the covariate-shift explanation directly. Verify evaluator convergence with a finer grid on the test rows whose success differences are reported.

[paper-level] Compute from the stored score vectors the pre-registered top-2 near-tie fraction and the teacher noise-floor regret (if computable from existing labels). Report total training compute, including teacher labelling, and a per-seed variance decomposition of the H2 interval.

[paper-level] Analyse the g_T vs grid-BI inversion on existing test3 episodes: report the per-episode correlation, the ordering by probe count, and how often histories rank differently under each measure. This turns C3 from an observation into an explained finding.
[paper-level] Restate the latency decomposition precisely. Account for the ~0.06 s of G* time not attributed to the three components, and give the pruning ceiling under both attributions.

[paper-level] Reframe the title, abstract and contributions around what the data support: a characterisation of a stay-and-probe regime, a caution about contrastive proxy objectives, and the budget confound in planner distillation. Drop or soften the implied amortization answer.

[paper-level] Rewrite the abstract and introduction for readability. State each finding once, in plain terms, and move gate thresholds, interval bookkeeping and repeated qualifiers to Sections 4, 7 and Appendix A.
